Negeri Sembilan was once one of Malaysia’s poorest states, rooted deeply in labor-intensive agriculture like rubber and tin mining. Its luck changed dramatically with the expansion of the Klang Valley, KLIA, and the PLUS highway. Today, its growth is powered by the Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0) mega-plan—an area double the size of Singapore—that focuses on high-tech industries. This blueprint is transforming the state into a hub for aerospace, semiconductors, and AI-integrated logistics.

This video maps out the six main development parcels of MVV 2.0, from the new High-Tech Industrial Park in Nilai to the upcoming AI Smart Container Port in Port Dickson. We look at the Sunway Seremban Sentral TOD project, major investments from global firms like Safran and Samsung SDI (EV batteries), and the RM1.8 billion F&N megafarm that will boost Malaysia's food security. Negeri Sembilan is not just expanding; it’s building a modern, high-tech, and digitally connected economy right next door to KL.
